issue_context.title: netty nextReceiveBufferSize bug
issue_context.body:
I think netty's dynamic memory computing may be a bug, please see netty source code ``AdaptiveRecvByteBufAllocator.HandleImpl#record``, if ``actualReadBytes`` is 2155, the final result of var ``nextReceiveBufferSize`` should be 4196, but the reality is that it will always 8192,
the reason is that var ``index``  is reduced by one, but if judged it will continue to be subtracted by one.
please see my example code. on branch `` netty_bug_demo`` ,executing my sample code console will print memory allocation information.
run NettyServer and NettyClient .
https://github.com/brucelwl/demo/tree/netty_bug_demo

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13413715/64473965-e300da80-d19f-11e9-9810-bc5e832f443d.png)
comments: @johnou @normanmaurer  Why is no one confirming this issue?
@brucelwl to be honest I don't think the unit test is up to snuff, plus waiting for feedback from @trustin

review_comments: Can we also assert the guess incrementing after the read bytes increases?
yes, But I think my unit test is correct.
I'm not saying it's incorrect, but it only asserts in one direction.
Maybe method ``rampUpBeforeReadCompleteWhenLargeDataPending`` contains the assertions you need.
Point was to test going down and up to ensure the predicted buffer size is adaptive.
After playing with this a bit I feel the unit test is flawed as it does not take into consideration the index increment and decrement step.
